names.legendary: Aperturion, Collector of Lost Seconds

lore.common: Captures everyone's blink with surgical precision. Family albums are its trophy room.
lore.uncommon: Sets off its flash only when somebody announces they don't want a picture.
lore.rare: Photographs the moment before something happens. Its last image showed a cake on the floor and nobody trusts it now.
lore.epic: Stole every flash of lightning in a summer storm to create one photograph. The resulting family portrait included seventeen confused clouds.
lore.legendary: Aperturion has photographed every moment history forgot. Once it opened its shutter for a second too long, and an entire afternoon disappeared into the lens.

names.legendary: Opticarus, Eye Beyond the Horizon

lore.common: Grows a perfect fingerprint right in the centre the second someone cleans it.
lore.uncommon: Zooms toward every embarrassing detail in the room. The family has banned portraits.
lore.rare: Makes distant mountains look close enough to touch. One tourist tried and startled a very annoyed goat.
lore.epic: Focused a single sunbeam so precisely that it burned the words NICE TRY onto a cloud. Meteorologists refuse to discuss it.
lore.legendary: Opticarus sees the secrets hidden between starlight and dust. It once magnified a grain of sand until an entire civilisation asked to be left alone.

names.legendary: Cinemor, Director of Unwritten Worlds

lore.common: Makes everybody repeat the same entrance fifteen times. Forgot to press record.
lore.uncommon: Demands absolute silence, then loudly eats a sandwich during the take.
lore.rare: Shouts CUT in the director's voice whenever somebody is about to say something embarrassing.
lore.epic: Filmed an action scene so grand that the entire city began behaving like extras. Even the traffic lights waited for their cue.
lore.legendary: Cinemor films histories that have not happened yet. Every century one reel escapes its vault, and the stars must decide whether to play their assigned parts.

names.legendary: Daguerra, Collector of Unborn Pictures

lore.common: Runs out of film at the most important moment and photographs the photographer's shoes.
lore.uncommon: Needs winding after every shot, but acts as if winding is beneath it.
lore.rare: Develops one photograph from tomorrow on every roll. The rest are of somebody's thumb.
lore.epic: Captured the town parade on a single roll of film, then released the people from the photographs into the darkroom. The marching band refused to leave.
lore.legendary: Daguerra took the last portrait of a city before it was lost to the sea. Each full moon, its silver negatives reveal one more street and the people who used to dance there.

names.legendary: Premonisha, Photographer of Tomorrow

lore.common: Spits out a picture and watches everyone shake it despite the instructions.
lore.uncommon: Prints a photo precisely when someone has finally stopped posing.
lore.rare: Captures a person's thoughts instead of their face. Every family portrait is mostly about dinner.
lore.epic: Printed a hundred portraits during a wedding, each showing what the guests would look like after eating the cake. The baker demanded a retake.
lore.legendary: Premonisha took a photograph of the first snowfall a week before winter arrived. The village prepared in time, and every year the snow sends her a thank-you card.

names.legendary: Capriccio, Keeper of the Unseen Shot

lore.common: Refuses to leave the camera lens just when the perfect photograph appears.
lore.uncommon: Swings from its tether and bonks the photographer's nose with artistic confidence.
lore.rare: Vanishes into a pocket containing absolutely nothing else, then turns up inside a shoe.
lore.epic: Rolled down a mountain during the holiday photo, leading an entire hiking party into a cafe on the far side. Every picture shows only their running feet.
lore.legendary: Capriccio kept the lens covered during the rarest eclipse in a thousand years. When the photographer finally removed it, the picture showed not darkness, but a thousand stars nobody had ever seen.

names.legendary: Camerathos, the Witness of Lost Hours

lore.common: Runs out of power exactly when the birthday candles go out.
lore.uncommon: Tilts every wedding video until the horizon looks seasick.
lore.rare: Rewinds a recording just far enough to expose who stole the last cupcake.
lore.epic: Filmed the school play with its lens cap on, then projected the actors' shadows so perfectly that the audience demanded a second show.
lore.legendary: Recorded a deserted town for one night and captured the laughter of everyone who had ever lived there. The film runs only when someone remembers their names.

names.legendary: Televisionax, the Window of Elsewhere

lore.common: Ignores the remote until its owner stands up. It has excellent comic timing.
lore.uncommon: Can make the entire family forget why they entered the living room.
lore.rare: Changes to the cooking channel at dinner time. The chef on screen is always eating something better.
lore.epic: Showed a football so realistically that the whole neighbourhood dived onto their sofas. The furniture shops had their best week in history.
lore.legendary: Televisionax once displayed a window into a kingdom where every television watched humans. The viewers stared back for an hour before both sides changed the channel in embarrassment.

names.legendary: King Respawn, Warden of Lost Weekends

lore.common: Starts a giant update the moment you want to play.
lore.uncommon: Moves the character a little to the left whenever its owner lets go of the controller. Claims the joystick is haunted.
lore.rare: Knows the exact moment before a boss is defeated and chooses that moment to crash.
lore.epic: Announced a ten-minute update at the start of a tournament. By the time it finished, the spectators had grandchildren.
lore.legendary: King Respawn can restart any battle but never the weekend lost playing it. Those who defeat him earn a trophy shaped like a neglected laundry basket.

names.legendary: Farsight the Round-the-World

lore.common: Has a strap that bumps against your chest on every step.
lore.uncommon: Is held the wrong way round by everyone the first time, making everything tiny.
lore.rare: Makes everything look so close that its owner keeps ducking whenever a bird flies past a mile away.
lore.epic: Was lent to a short-sighted owl at the nature reserve, and the owl has refused to give them back ever since.
lore.legendary: Looked so far into the distance that it saw all the way round the world to the back of its owner's own head.

names.legendary: Pharos, the Unblinking Star

lore.common: Blinks all night outside the bedroom window. Nobody has convinced it that bedtime applies to lights.
lore.uncommon: Sits on a rocking buoy and sends secret messages to fishing boats. Most translate as HELLO DUCKS.
lore.rare: Flashes in a pattern that summons every gull in the harbour. The fish market has begged it to change the password.
lore.epic: Split a black thunderhead with a single shaft of light and guided an entire lost fleet home through the gap.
lore.legendary: When every lighthouse was dark, Pharos lit the ocean from beneath the waves. Sailors still chart their courses by that impossible flame.

names.legendary: Sequenzor, King of the Last Beat

lore.common: Loops the same four notes until somebody offers it a better hobby.
lore.uncommon: Adds a cowbell to every track, including lullabies and funerals.
lore.rare: Speeds up the beat by one step each minute. Nobody at the wedding has stopped dancing since Thursday.
lore.epic: Locked an entire city into one irresistible dance rhythm. The traffic lights began flashing in time and the parking meters demanded solos.
lore.legendary: Sequenzor programmed a dance so infectious that the royal palace refused to stop moving for a year. The king now issues decrees by moonwalking through the throne room.

names.legendary: Harmonia, Breath of the Old Chapel

lore.common: Needs pumping before it can sing, and sounds offended by every push.
lore.uncommon: Holds one note so long that the pianist has enough time to make tea.
lore.rare: Breathes in a whole page of sheet music and plays the tune from memory. Occasionally substitutes a shopping list.
lore.epic: Filled the village hall with an enormous humming chord. The windows vibrated and all the pigeons on the roof bowed.
lore.legendary: Harmonia once played through a winter when no choir could reach the chapel. Its reeds carried the villagers' voices over the snow until spring.

names.legendary: Keytarion, the Electric Showman

lore.common: Hangs from its musician like an oversized tie with stage fright.
lore.uncommon: Glows brighter each time somebody asks whether it is a guitar or a piano.
lore.rare: Plays the wedding march as a blistering solo. The bride now enters on a skateboard.
lore.epic: Climbed the stage speakers for a solo so spectacular that the entire front row grew matching mullets.
lore.legendary: Keytarion struck a chord that split the night into seven neon colours. The northern lights applied to join its backing band and were told to practise their scales.

names.legendary: Maestro Faderon, Lord of Lost Echoes

lore.common: Moves exactly one slider when the sound engineer looks away. Always the one labelled DO NOT TOUCH.
lore.uncommon: Blinks its hundreds of buttons like a tiny spaceship trying to flirt with the drummer.
lore.rare: Gives the worst singer a heavenly voice and the best singer a kazoo. Claims this is balance.
lore.epic: Turned one goose honk into the festival's bass drop. The entire crowd began dancing and nobody could convince the goose it was not the headliner.
lore.legendary: Faderon mixed the voices of a thousand vanished performances into a single concert. At the final note, the echoes returned to applaud the performers they had outlived.

names.legendary: Gramophonia, Spirit of the Last Waltz

lore.common: Skips the same lyric until everybody knows it by heart.
lore.uncommon: Adds a dramatic crackle to songs that never asked for one.
lore.rare: Calls a forgotten singer's voice out of an old record as if the recording were new.
lore.epic: Spun a century of dance music in one night, making every person in the ballroom dance backwards through their own fashions.
lore.legendary: Gramophonia guards the final recording of a vanished orchestra. On the first snowfall each year, the musicians appear as silhouettes and play one last waltz.

names.legendary: Syntheria, Composer of Unheard Worlds

lore.common: Plays a duck noise whenever the musician selects grand piano.
lore.uncommon: Changes the instrument halfway through a love song. The wedding guests were not expecting bagpipes.
lore.rare: Shapes soundwaves into tiny glowing animals that hop across the keyboard.
lore.epic: Played a bass note so enormous that the concert's holographic skyline became real for one very confused encore.
lore.legendary: Syntheria knows the music hidden between frequencies. Her first composition gave the northern lights a rhythm; her last is still waiting to be played.

names.legendary: Wikkara, Spinner of the Missing Song

lore.common: Skips at the very best part of the record and blames the dust.
lore.uncommon: Spins backwards whenever someone says that music was better years ago.
lore.rare: Scratches a record so cleverly that forgotten voices join the chorus from the groove.
lore.epic: Turned an empty ballroom into a whirling dance floor where chairs, coats and the chandelier all performed a perfect disco routine.
lore.legendary: Wikkara keeps the last copy of every melody that has vanished from the world. When her needle touches the silent vinyl, even people who have forgotten how to dance remember the steps.

names.legendary: Luminox, False Sun of the Upstairs Hall

lore.common: Collects tiny moths inside its shade and demands that somebody admire the collection.
lore.uncommon: Flickers every time someone mentions replacing it. It is pretending to be sentimental.
lore.rare: Goes dark the moment a person sits comfortably, then lights up when they stand to investigate.
lore.epic: Blazed so brightly over the neighbourhood that every rooster crowed at midnight. The council sent it a bill for an additional sunrise.
lore.legendary: Luminox shines with a light stolen from the dawn. Night and day both claim ownership, so he settles their argument with a very irritating flicker.

names.legendary: Crystallith, Crown of the Hanging Stars

lore.common: Clinks whenever somebody closes a door. The house insists it was gentle.
lore.uncommon: Collects dust on a thousand crystals and sends one sparkle to hide the evidence.
lore.rare: Reflects everything said at the dinner table into miniature scenes on the ceiling. Gossip has become dangerous.
lore.epic: Turned the royal ballroom into a storm of reflected suns. Every dancer wore sunglasses at midnight and called it fashionable.
lore.legendary: Crystallith hangs from the ceiling of the oldest palace, lit by captive starlight. When it rings, even thunder falls silent to hear the next note.

names.legendary: Lustrella, Matchmaker of the Golden Hall

lore.common: Keeps one bulb slightly dimmer than the others. Refuses to identify the culprit.
lore.uncommon: Sways whenever someone walks upstairs and insists the building is dancing.
lore.rare: Changes its glow to match a guest's secret crush. Dinner parties become extremely informative.
lore.epic: Dimmed every light at the grand banquet exactly as a surprise proposal began. Three unrelated couples proposed to the wrong people.
lore.legendary: Lustrella once arranged a romance between two rival stars using nothing but perfect lighting. She has been forbidden from meddling in royal marriages, a rule she ignores nightly.

names.legendary: Luminara, Lamp of the Last Scholar

lore.common: Bends its neck to shine straight into the reader's eyes.
lore.uncommon: Attracts moths who treat every homework assignment as a dance floor.
lore.rare: Highlights embarrassing typos while leaving the correct answers in darkness.
lore.epic: Lit the entire exam hall so brightly that even the invigilators could read everyone's secret notes.
lore.legendary: Has burned beside the world's greatest thinkers across a thousand sleepless nights. Its one regret is illuminating the moment someone invented the reply-all email.

names.legendary: Lankarius, Guardian of the Reading Nook

lore.common: Is taller than the sofa and spends its evenings looking down on everyone.
lore.uncommon: Has a foot switch in exactly the place people tread while carrying tea.
lore.rare: Leans over every reader like an inquisitive detective. Has solved fourteen crossword puzzles.
lore.epic: Cast a shadow so immense at the dinner party that guests believed a giant was standing in the garden. The actual giant sent a letter of complaint.
lore.legendary: Lankarius lit the last library after a citywide blackout, letting a thousand readers finish their stories. The librarians still knit it a new cardigan each winter.

names.legendary: Tallulah, the Lighthouse on Three Legs

lore.common: Wobbles whenever somebody breathes near its three skinny legs.
lore.uncommon: Moves its shadow behind the photographer so every portrait looks like it has a secret guest.
lore.rare: Lights faces from below at precisely the wrong moment, turning wedding portraits into ghost stories.
lore.epic: Extended itself above the stage and lit the entire outdoor concert from a single spotlight. The moths demanded front-row tickets.
lore.legendary: Tallulah stood on a cliff when the old lighthouse went dark, stretching her three legs into the clouds. Ships still find their way by the glow that waits on her highest rung.

names.legendary: Penduluna, Lantern of the Lost Banquet

lore.common: Hangs at the exact height of an unsuspecting forehead. Bonk is its favourite greeting.
lore.uncommon: Swings when anyone sneezes, turning dinner into a very small lighthouse tour.
lore.rare: Follows a mysterious guest around the table with a beam of light, even after the bulb is switched off.
lore.epic: Descended over a royal feast and spotlighted every stolen dessert. The entire court confessed before the pudding course.
lore.legendary: Penduluna hung above a banquet that lasted one hundred years. Her gentle glow kept every guest young until the final candle was blown out.

names.legendary: Illuminara, Lantern of Unfinished Tales

lore.common: Clips to the page, then slips off whenever the plot gets exciting.
lore.uncommon: Shines directly into the eyes of anyone trying to sleep beside the reader.
lore.rare: Lights a hidden message between the lines of old storybooks, but only after midnight.
lore.epic: Beamed every unfinished book in the library onto the night sky. The entire town stayed awake trying to find out what happened next.
lore.legendary: Illuminara guided a lost storyteller through a century of darkness, illuminating one page at a time. Every book it touches gains an ending that nobody remembers writing.

names.legendary: Lumivela, Halo of the Unseen Star

lore.common: Gives every photograph two glowing rings in the eyes and nobody an excuse.
lore.uncommon: Makes the family cat look like a professional model, then refuses to photograph humans.
lore.rare: Illuminates the truth behind every flattering filter during the live stream.
lore.epic: Turned every face in the studio into a perfect porcelain portrait. The cast refused to come off camera for a week.
lore.legendary: Lumivela once shone on a forgotten singer whose voice no audience had heard. Her light drew a crowd beneath the night sky, and the first concert began.

names.legendary: Solara, the Second Sun of the Stage

lore.common: Makes actors shine under pressure. Mostly on their foreheads.
lore.uncommon: Wraps every face in flattering light, even the grumpy sound engineer's.
lore.rare: Moves the shadows around a set so convincingly that the villain gets lost in his own entrance.
lore.epic: Lit an entire film set so fiercely that the cardboard castle cast a shadow over the real city. The director kept the shot.
lore.legendary: Solara illuminated the first performance beneath a moonless sky, turning a humble travelling stage into a sunrise that even distant sailors could see.

names.legendary: Lucernia, the Welcome at the Door

lore.common: Hides its switch exactly where a sleepy hand cannot find it.
lore.uncommon: Hums one note until everyone in the hall starts humming along.
lore.rare: Flicks on when someone raids the biscuit tin after bedtime.
lore.epic: Lit an abandoned hotel corridor so warmly that every ghost booked a room. They left excellent reviews but hated the early checkout.
lore.legendary: Burned through a century of dark nights beside a lonely mountain doorway. Travellers who saw its glow always found shelter before the snow reached them.

names.legendary: Lampwick, the Second Moon

lore.common: Squeaks its handle at every step, turning a stealthy walk into a creaky parade.
lore.uncommon: Hides its flame from the wind like a tiny nervous dragon.
lore.rare: Projects a shadow so enormous the hedgerow ducks when it passes.
lore.epic: Called every moth in the forest to follow a school night walk. By morning the classroom curtains had grown wings.
lore.legendary: Lampwick burned on the night the moon disappeared from the sky. Sailors followed its tiny flame into safe harbours, and the moon returned at dawn with a grateful silver wink.

names.legendary: Wattsworth, Keeper of the First Spark

lore.common: Pops exactly when somebody settles down with a good book.
lore.uncommon: Hums to itself inside the lampshade until the whole room wants to join in.
lore.rare: Glows above anyone thinking up a new idea, which makes surprise parties impossible.
lore.epic: Invented a new kind of light during the school play and illuminated every secret hiding place backstage. The villains had to improvise.
lore.legendary: Wattsworth captured the first clever thought ever thought by candlelight and held it safely in glass. Whenever someone loses hope, one tiny filament begins to glow again.

names.legendary: Pixelorius, the Eye of Infinite Screens

lore.common: Puts one dead pixel directly over whatever you're trying to read. It insists the dot is a design feature.
lore.uncommon: Gradually tips its head forward all afternoon. Calls the resulting neck pain an ergonomic lesson.
lore.rare: Opens windows no one remembers clicking. Some of them look out on places that do not exist.
lore.epic: Turned every screen in the office into a window onto the boss's secret gnome collection. The gnomes stared back and began holding performance reviews.
lore.legendary: Pixelorius once displayed every sunrise in the world at the same time. For one impossible minute, even the people in windowless rooms remembered what daylight looked like.

names.legendary: Panopticus, the Screen That Never Blinks

lore.common: Shows a dark corridor so grainy that the guard mistakes a mop for a burglar.
lore.uncommon: Divides the world into sixteen tiny boxes and insists on checking each one before breakfast.
lore.rare: Shows the empty room that somebody will enter five minutes later. The night guard has stopped being surprised.
lore.epic: Displayed a different pigeon on every screen at once. The entire security team chased them, only to discover one extremely talented pigeon.
lore.legendary: Panopticus watched an empty room for a thousand nights until the room itself began watching back. Nobody on the night shift has agreed to explain what appeared on the seventeenth screen.

names.legendary: Discoria, Keeper of Ten Thousand Songs

lore.common: Skips past your favourite track every time your thumb touches the wheel.
lore.uncommon: Braids its earbud wires together in a pocket with absolutely no help.
lore.rare: Chooses the most embarrassing song in your library exactly as the headphones unplug on the bus.
lore.epic: Connected itself to the school speakers during an emergency drill. The entire class evacuated in disco formation.
lore.legendary: Discoria gathered the favourite song of every traveller who ever rode the night train. Her little silver wheel still plays the lost voices between stations.

names.legendary: Nanobelle, the Indestructible Playlist

lore.common: Clips to a sleeve and immediately disappears beneath the cuff.
lore.uncommon: Resembles a packet of chewing gum so convincingly that it gets offered to strangers.
lore.rare: Plays a song with precisely the wrong jogging rhythm and turns every sprint into skipping.
lore.epic: Led a charity race with a march so infectious that every runner, dog and spectator finished in perfect step. The mayor requested an encore.
lore.legendary: Nanobelle survived seven spins in a washing machine and emerged still playing. Some say the bubbles in her songs contain melodies that have not been written yet.

names.legendary: Megabeat, Keeper of Forgotten Songs

lore.common: Keeps enough charge for one more song and refuses to say which one.
lore.uncommon: Plays the same tune seventeen times, then acts surprised when somebody sings along in their sleep.
lore.rare: Slips an old sea shanty into every playlist. The owner now knows how to hoist a mainsail.
lore.epic: Played a forgotten road-trip mixtape that made the whole family relive the holiday in reverse. They arrived home feeling ten years younger and desperate for snacks.
lore.legendary: Megabeat preserves songs no living person remembers. When its ancient headphones are plugged in at midnight, entire vanished dance halls return for one last chorus.

names.legendary: Professor Glassglow of the Sky Lesson

lore.common: Hums over the lesson like an elderly wasp that has learned algebra.
lore.uncommon: Shows every transparency backwards, then acts hurt when the teacher turns it around.
lore.rare: Makes a shadow of the smallest hand look enormous enough to frighten the class pet.
lore.epic: Projected the day's weather onto the school ceiling so convincingly that the pupils opened umbrellas indoors. The maths teacher called it practical geometry.
lore.legendary: Professor Glassglow projected the stars of a lost constellation onto a village wall. Sailors used the glowing chart to find the way home long after the observatory had fallen.

names.legendary: Luminarch, Weaver of Living Light

lore.common: Projects an enormous blurry cat onto the neighbour's wall. Nobody knows whose cat it is.
lore.uncommon: Makes every presentation look impressive until someone tries to read the tiny text.
lore.rare: Projects shadows that step off the screen and quietly rearrange the furniture.
lore.epic: Beamed a sea monster onto the harbour fog. The navy spent three days negotiating with a very convincing light show.
lore.legendary: Luminarch projected the first sunrise onto a cave wall for a people who had never seen the sky. The painted dawn still rises each night in its darkness.

names.legendary: Solfilia, Heart of the Silver Screen

lore.common: Glows fiercely until the movie reaches its best scene, then winks out.
lore.uncommon: Heats up so much during presentations that the lecturer could toast bread beside it.
lore.rare: Enlarges even the tiniest dust mote into a terrifying shadow monster on the screen.
lore.epic: Burned so brightly during the premiere that the actors' shadows escaped the screen and demanded an encore.
lore.legendary: Solfilia has burned inside a hundred cinemas without ever dimming. Every film she illuminates leaves one star behind in the audience's dreams.

names.legendary: Carousella, Queen of Vanished Summers

lore.common: Jams on the photograph of a blurry thumb and refuses to show the mountains.
lore.uncommon: Projects Grandad upside down in every holiday slideshow, to the family's delight.
lore.rare: Brings the smell of salt air and sunscreen into the living room when it shows an old beach holiday.
lore.epic: Projected a slideshow so vivid that a herd of pictured goats trotted across the wall and ate the curtains. The host ended the evening early.
lore.legendary: Carousella holds summer afternoons from people long since gone in tiny framed pieces of light. Each click lets a family visit one beloved day again before the lamp grows dim.

names.legendary: Radiocron, Tyrant of the Sixth Hour

lore.common: Moves its snooze button exactly half an inch away every morning. Tiny evil.
lore.uncommon: Tunes itself to weather reports when you wanted music. It takes criticism personally.
lore.rare: Plays tomorrow's news at full volume. The sports results have ruined several bets.
lore.epic: Broadcast a single wake-up call so loud that every commuter arrived at work an hour early. The economy briefly improved; morale did not.
lore.legendary: Radiocron commands the minute before dawn, when all dreams should end. One day it overslept, and the entire kingdom enjoyed the first Monday without a morning.

names.legendary: Transistor Tess, Voice of Tomorrow

lore.common: Pokes the picnic guests with its telescopic antenna whenever the music gets good.
lore.uncommon: Tunes itself to a station playing the one song its owner cannot stand.
lore.rare: Catches broadcasts from faraway coastlines when the batteries are nearly empty.
lore.epic: Hijacked every radio along the beach with a forgotten song, sending a thousand strangers dancing together at sunset.
lore.legendary: Transistor Tess received a warning from a storm that had not yet formed. The fishing fleet returned safely, and the radio still hums tomorrow's weather at dawn.

names.legendary: Radiomancer, Speaker of Unheard Songs

lore.common: Crackles during the best line of every song, then works perfectly during the adverts.
lore.uncommon: Changes stations when nobody is looking and pretends the static did it.
lore.rare: Tunes into conversations carried by distant storms, then plays them back as weather reports.
lore.epic: Broadcast a single dance tune through every kitchen radio in the country. The traffic reports became a national conga line.
lore.legendary: Radiomancer once heard a song travelling between distant stars and played it to a lonely lighthouse keeper. Its melody still returns whenever the sea is calm.

names.legendary: Cassettara, Keeper of the Unheard Song

lore.common: Spills its magnetic guts into the player and blames the machine.
lore.uncommon: Can only be rewound with a pencil. It refuses pens on artistic grounds.
lore.rare: Slows a song down whenever it senses someone enjoying themselves. The singer sounds like a sleepy walrus.
lore.epic: Played a forgotten side B so loudly that the entire coach trip turned into Dad's bagpipe recital. The driver demanded a new career.
lore.legendary: Cassettara keeps recordings of concerts that were never performed. Once rewound beyond the beginning of music and captured the sound of a dinosaur humming.

names.legendary: Lord Valvethunder, the Last Encore

lore.common: Hums quietly until a guitarist touches the cable, then screams as though stepped on.
lore.uncommon: Has eleven volume settings. All eleven make the neighbours knock on the wall.
lore.rare: Summons a squeal of feedback that sends pigeons into perfect musical formation.
lore.epic: Turned up one guitar solo until the garage door unlatched, the car rolled away and the band's drummer begged to join it.
lore.legendary: Lord Valvethunder has not switched off since the first rock concert. His eternal chord echoes beneath the hills, where the sheep keep remarkably good time.

names.legendary: Karaokina, the Star-Maker of the Shy

lore.common: Turns every confident singer into a squeaking kettle by the second verse.
lore.uncommon: Applauds even the most dreadful song, then demands an encore from the embarrassed singer.
lore.rare: Scrolls the lyrics a line ahead, making the whole room sing an entirely different chorus.
lore.epic: Gave the neighbour's cat a perfect score at the talent show. The cat now insists on performing three encores a night.
lore.legendary: Karaokina once gave a timid child the courage to sing before a silent kingdom. One note broke the silence, and the halls have echoed with music ever since.

names.legendary: Sonoria, Voice Beneath the Mountains

lore.common: Turns footsteps in a film into dinosaur stomps and actual dinosaurs into quiet little squeaks.
lore.uncommon: Whispers from behind the sofa until the family checks for hidden actors.
lore.rare: Steals all the dialogue but amplifies every biscuit wrapper, forcing the cinema to provide subtitles for snacks.
lore.epic: Let out one bass note so deep that every cupboard in the neighbourhood opened and the crockery applauded.
lore.legendary: Sonoria sings in frequencies that only mountains understand. When she hums a lullaby, sleeping volcanoes smile in their dreams.

names.legendary: Voxar, the Mountain's Lost Voice

lore.common: Plays the first note of your favourite song whenever you're trying to sneak out quietly.
lore.uncommon: Pairs with the neighbour's phone and announces their embarrassing playlist across the garden.
lore.rare: Can steal an echo from any room and make it sing harmonies three seconds ahead of the music.
lore.epic: Boomed so powerfully at a rock concert that the stage marched itself into the audience, still performing.
lore.legendary: Voxar once swallowed a thunderclap whole. Every hundred years he releases a single note, and the mountains answer in perfect harmony.

names.legendary: General Megavox, the Thunder Herald

lore.common: Turns a simple 'hello' into a noise that frightens the pigeons off the roof.
lore.uncommon: Gives an ear-splitting squeal whenever someone points it toward a speaker.
lore.rare: Announces whispers loudly enough for the whole school to learn who stole the final biscuit.
lore.epic: Shouted the opening instructions at the village sports day and sent the competitors running before the referee had arrived.
lore.legendary: General Megavox once called across a mountain range to warn of an avalanche. A hundred villages heard his voice, but the snow obeyed and stood still.

names.legendary: Admiral Bellows, Voice of the Coast

lore.common: Honks from the pier just as the seagulls are settling down for a nap.
lore.uncommon: Makes the lifeguard sound like an angry robot asking everyone to walk.
lore.rare: Calls the lost boats home through fog so thick their lanterns cannot be seen.
lore.epic: Announced the ice-cream van over the harbour loudspeakers and caused a flotilla of fishing boats to race toward shore.
lore.legendary: Admiral Bellows gave voice to a silent lighthouse during the longest sea fog. Every vessel reached safe water by following his echo through the dark.

names.legendary: Highscoreth, the Eternal Game Master

lore.common: Eats coins and gives out exactly three seconds of fun. It has never received a good customer review.
lore.uncommon: Moves the joystick one pixel left at the worst moment. Blames the player's skill level.
lore.rare: Lives inside the high-score screen and replaces every champion's name with its own. Players have started signing as AAA out of spite.
lore.epic: Escaped its cabinet and summoned every final boss in the arcade at once. The city was saved by a grandmother who knew the cheat code.
lore.legendary: Highscoreth built a maze of infinite levels behind the last pixel. Those who beat its final challenge earn one prize: a free retry, and the dreadful knowledge that there was never a final level.

names.legendary: Creditorix, Keeper of the Golden Zero

lore.common: Whispers the wrong PIN into your ear just as you reach the keypad. Has a very punchable little face.
lore.uncommon: Prints receipts long enough to wrap around the building. Insists you might need them for tax purposes.
lore.rare: Dispenses entire handfuls of tiny coins and laughs as you count them. Bankers have classified it as a natural hazard.
lore.epic: Opened every cash slot in the city at once and unleashed a blizzard of banknotes. The pigeons immediately founded a stock exchange.
lore.legendary: Creditorix guards the mythical account containing the world's first coin. It can make kings rich with a keystroke, but still charges a fee for checking your balance.

names.legendary: Jukeline, the Last Keeper of Vinyl

lore.common: Swallows a coin and plays the wrong song with complete confidence.
lore.uncommon: Glows in rainbow neon while everyone else in the diner argues over the playlist.
lore.rare: Knows the song a visitor misses most and plays it before they even touch the buttons.
lore.epic: Started a rock-and-roll riot in the diner, pulling every chair onto the dance floor. The milkshakes formed a chorus line.
lore.legendary: Jukeline holds a record cut from the first song ever sung in that town. When it plays at midnight, the empty streets fill with the footsteps of dancers long gone.

names.legendary: Sir Snapstrip, Archivist of Faces

lore.common: Takes its first picture at the exact moment you sit down and make a startled face.
lore.uncommon: Flashes four times, then prints four slightly different versions of your closed eyes.
lore.rare: Sneaks an unfamiliar smiling figure into every photo. Nobody has ever seen it outside the booth.
lore.epic: Photographed every guest at a royal wedding in one impossible strip. The bride discovered a very proud dragon standing between her parents.
lore.legendary: Sir Snapstrip squeezes one future cousin into every family photo. Genealogists have queued outside its little curtain for forty years, and the cousins keep growing moustaches.

names.legendary: Fortuna Fruitwheel, the Lady of Chance

lore.common: Spins three lemons and acts terribly proud of its sour performance.
lore.uncommon: Rings a bell every time somebody walks past, whether it has been played or not.
lore.rare: Makes its fruit symbols appear on nearby wallpaper, socks and sandwich wrappers.
lore.epic: Turned the entire arcade into a spinning orchard of cherries and lemons. The owner had to hire a gardener instead of a technician.
lore.legendary: Fortuna Fruitwheel can make a thousand reels stop in perfect alignment, but she saves her luck for the people who never ask for it. Her greatest prize was the return of a lost pier dog.

names.legendary: Terminus Rex, Printer of Lost Stops

lore.common: Prints a ticket exactly when the train doors close. It considers this impeccable timing.
lore.uncommon: Eats the one coin you have left and coughs up a receipt for emotional damages.
lore.rare: Issues fares to stations erased from every map; passengers return with unfamiliar accents and excellent pastries.
lore.epic: Printed a ticket that unrolled through twelve carriages, tied the conductor's ankles and dragged the entire train into an unscheduled sightseeing tour.
lore.legendary: Terminus Rex prints one golden ticket each century to a platform between yesterday and tomorrow. The passengers return older, wiser and oddly certain their luggage has been judging them.

names.legendary: Vendetta, the Midnight Concierge

lore.common: Lets a chocolate bar hang off the spiral just to watch the disappointment.
lore.uncommon: Ignores the first five taps and responds to the sixth with a sigh.
lore.rare: Knows whether you need coffee or a biscuit and always dispenses the opposite.
lore.epic: Shook loose all its snacks during an office emergency. By dawn the lobby had become a biscuit-based government with crisps in charge.
lore.legendary: Opens only for people who genuinely need cheering up. Its secret menu changes every night, but a hot cocoa for a lonely night-shift worker is always free.

names.legendary: Omnix, Eye of the Last Horizon

lore.common: Clings to helmets and narrates every bicycle wobble like the final battle of an ancient war.
lore.uncommon: Its single glass eye stays open underwater. It insists that pond algae are an undiscovered civilisation.
lore.rare: Attaches itself to birds and films places no human has visited. Its last recording ended inside a very confused seagull.
lore.epic: It did not film the mountain collapsing. The mountain collapsed to make Shutterquake's entrance.
lore.legendary: Every vanished expedition left behind flawless footage. In each recording, Omnix is visible filming from somewhere impossible.

names.legendary: Vigiluna, the Sleepless Eye

lore.common: Crackles whenever the nursery falls quiet. Parents have learned to fear its dramatic timing.
lore.uncommon: Amplifies every tiny snore into the sound of a sleeping dragon. The actual baby snores like a hamster.
lore.rare: Picks up lullabies from nurseries three streets away. Has accidentally raised seven families who don't know each other.
lore.epic: Broadcast a single midnight hiccup to every house in the village. Two hundred parents rushed upstairs at once, and every baby slept through it.
lore.legendary: Vigiluna watches over all sleeping children through a thousand tiny screens. No whisper escapes its hearing, though it still cannot explain where the missing dummy went.

names.legendary: Voltairex, Heart of the Machines

lore.common: Always goes into the remote backwards, even when the instructions are printed right there.
lore.uncommon: Hides among forty dead batteries in the kitchen drawer and pretends to be one of them.
lore.rare: Can wake a forgotten toy from twenty years ago. The toy remembers every embarrassing childhood nickname.
lore.epic: Brought every appliance in the city to life during a blackout. The toasters formed a union before breakfast.
lore.legendary: An ancient cell carrying the last spark of a vanished civilization. When Voltairex awakens, even abandoned robots remember their names.

names.legendary: Candelabrax, Monarch of the Dancing Dark

lore.common: Drips wax onto the expensive tablecloth and claims it is decorating.
lore.uncommon: Keeps five flames alive but never agrees which one should burn highest.
lore.rare: Commands the shadows cast by each candle. One shadow has been paying rent in the hallway.
lore.epic: Stretched five flickering shadows into towering dancers and seized the banquet hall. The orchestra played until the castle ran out of night.
lore.legendary: Candelabrax carries five flames stolen from the first stars. Each one illuminates a different century, so dinner guests often meet their descendants by candlelight.

names.legendary: Votivar, Guardian of the Last Vigil

lore.common: Collects wax drips like precious jewels. It will never let the table see them again.
lore.uncommon: Leans the candle just enough to make the wallpaper nervous.
lore.rare: Bends candle shadows into silent little people who follow visitors around the room.
lore.epic: Held a thousand candles upright through an earthquake while the castle spun around them. The candles complained about the draught.
lore.legendary: Votivar guarded one tiny flame through a thousand winter nights until the lost city found its way home. Now it demands that every guest bring their own candle.

names.legendary: Rewindex, Ghost of Lost Recorded Voices

lore.common: Hisses louder than the music. Claims the hiss is an important part of the arrangement.
lore.uncommon: Makes you turn it over exactly as the best song reaches its chorus.
lore.rare: Records over treasured memories with weather reports and adverts for vacuum cleaners. It calls this archival work.
lore.epic: Replaced every song at the school disco with the DJ's voice announcing them. Nobody danced, but his ego had a wonderful night.
lore.legendary: Rewindex holds every message someone recorded but never delivered. At midnight, its spools turn by themselves and a thousand forgotten voices sing along.

names.legendary: Compactron, Keeper of the Silver Song

lore.common: Skips exactly three seconds of your favourite song. Never the advertisements.
lore.uncommon: Throws rainbows onto the ceiling and is convinced it invented colour.
lore.rare: Remembers music so old that its player has forgotten how to open. The nostalgia is mutual.
lore.epic: Spun on the garden fence until thousands of magpies gathered for a disco beneath its flashing rainbow.
lore.legendary: Compactron stores every song ever played on a silver disc. One scratch in its armour erased a chart-topping hit from history, and nobody misses it.

names.legendary: Discoboros, the Six-Disc Paradox

lore.common: Clunks loudly between tracks as though rearranging heavy furniture in its stomach.
lore.uncommon: Insists on playing the same disc three times despite holding five others. Claims artistic direction.
lore.rare: Swaps the chorus of one song with another album's drum solo. The band sends a complaint.
lore.epic: Played six albums at once during the office party. The resulting sound made the printer begin breakdancing.
lore.legendary: Discoboros spins five ancient records around an empty sixth slot. Every full moon the missing album appears, containing songs nobody has written yet.

names.legendary: Plugzarius, Bringer of Lost Charge

lore.common: Works only when the cable is bent at an angle known to no branch of geometry.
lore.uncommon: Has the right plug for every device except the one that is currently dying.
lore.rare: Steals one percent of battery from every phone nearby to keep itself warm.
lore.epic: Connected every device in the house to a single socket and woke the smart fridge, which immediately ordered a hundred pizzas.
lore.legendary: Plugzarius can recharge a fallen star with one touch. Yet when asked to charge an ordinary phone, it solemnly announces that the accessory is not supported.

names.legendary: Vigilax, Eye of the Forgotten Road

lore.common: Records the entire drive but somehow misses the interesting part.
lore.uncommon: Falls from the windscreen at precisely the moment someone says Nice smooth road.
lore.rare: Knows who scratched the bumper, who stole the parking spot and who sang off-key in the car.
lore.epic: Broadcast a town's entire traffic history at once. Half the council immediately took the bus.
lore.legendary: Has witnessed every midnight road since the first wheel turned. Its tiny red light records journeys the drivers have forgotten, including one that hasn't happened yet.

names.legendary: Belladonna, Mistress of the Threshold

lore.common: Rings just as the shampoo reaches somebody's eyes.
lore.uncommon: Changes its tune every time the homeowner tries to recognize it.
lore.rare: Knows a delivery van is coming before its driver does. Demands a signature from the clouds.
lore.epic: Played every doorbell in the city as one enormous orchestra. The conductor was a confused postman holding forty parcels.
lore.legendary: One winter Belladonna rang at the doors of every lonely house, bringing an unexpected visitor to each. Nobody ever discovered who pressed the button.

names.legendary: Discovox, Archivist of Lost Evenings

lore.common: Plays the same menu music until the family starts singing along.
lore.uncommon: Freezes every movie on the worst possible facial expression.
lore.rare: Can bring a deleted scene back to life, usually one involving embarrassing dancing.
lore.epic: Released a director's cut so long that an entire film festival grew old watching it. The credits are still rolling in one theatre.
lore.legendary: Discovox holds the last copy of every story the world forgot. Once each winter it plays one on a moonlit wall for an audience that remembers being young.

names.legendary: Cordragon, the Endless Orange Coil

lore.common: Lies across the doorway and asks innocent questions after the third person trips.
lore.uncommon: Can tie itself into seventeen knots without ever leaving the cupboard.
lore.rare: Stretches under the garden fence to bring light to a secret hedgehog disco.
lore.epic: Uncoiled through the town fair and quietly connected every stall to the mayor's coffee machine. The machine demanded its own power station.
lore.legendary: When the winter darkness swallowed the valley, Cordragon carried a single lantern's light from cottage to cottage. Its tail still winds beneath the snow.

names.legendary: Shrilla, the Bell That Woke the King

lore.common: Shouts about burnt toast with the urgency of a dragon sighting.
lore.uncommon: Waits until three in the morning to request a new battery.
lore.rare: Can smell a suspicious candle from the far end of the corridor. It keeps a list.
lore.epic: Rang through the royal palace when the chef burned a single pancake. Every guard evacuated, and the king delivered a speech in his slippers.
lore.legendary: Shrilla once rang before the first flame reached a sleeping village. The villagers built a bell tower in its honour and still give it the ceremonial first slice of toast.

names.legendary: Sentinella, the Guardian of Last Embers

lore.common: Stands in the corner waiting to be useful. Practises looking important.
lore.uncommon: Has a safety pin that nobody may touch without a very good reason.
lore.rare: Can put out a dragon's sneeze before it reaches the curtains. The dragon is offended.
lore.epic: Unleashed a blizzard of foam to save the village fair from a runaway bonfire. The sausages survived, but the mayor emerged looking like a snowman.
lore.legendary: Sentinella once faced a wall of fire around an ancient library and opened a path through it. The rescued books still smell faintly of extinguishing foam and triumph.

names.legendary: Captain Smotherwell of the Red Order

lore.common: Has a tiny pressure gauge and insists everyone admire its needle.
lore.uncommon: Catches passing coats with its hose, then denies involvement.
lore.rare: Sneezes a little cloud of powder whenever anyone sings Happy Birthday.
lore.epic: At the fire drill, it covered the entire workshop in white dust before the first whistle. The workers had to be identified by their boots.
lore.legendary: Smotherwell once held the doorway while a whole castle evacuated a kitchen fire. The cook later knighted the red bottle with a wooden spoon.

names.legendary: Cellina, the Spark That Outlived Night

lore.common: Pretends to be full until the exact moment the power goes out.
lore.uncommon: Rolls under the sofa whenever someone opens the torch.
lore.rare: Can provide one final burst of light at the sight of a spider, then retires immediately.
lore.epic: Quit during the climax of the campsite ghost story. The entire camp screamed, including the ghost, who had not finished his lines.
lore.legendary: Cellina kept a lighthouse torch burning through a century of storms. When its final charge faded, the grateful keeper installed it beside the lamp as a tiny silver monument.

names.legendary: Luxander, Lantern of the Last Door

lore.common: Always rolls off the bedside table and shines directly into someone's eyes.
lore.uncommon: Makes a face look terrifying when held under the chin. The face belongs to a very confused grandad.
lore.rare: Can reveal the shadow of something that is not in the room. Nobody wants to check the cupboard.
lore.epic: Lit up an abandoned castle during the village ghost hunt. Every ghost froze in the beam and pretended to be a coat stand.
lore.legendary: Luxander followed the last lost child through a moonless forest, its beam cutting a safe path between the trees. Even the monsters under the roots stepped aside to let them pass.

names.legendary: Sir Floppimus, Keeper of Lost Saves

lore.common: Has a little metal shutter that everyone slides back and forth instead of doing homework.
lore.uncommon: Looks like the save icon but insists it was famous first.
lore.rare: Can hold an entire computer game, provided the game is mostly squares and imagination.
lore.epic: Clunked in every school computer at once, summoning a choir of ancient loading noises. The children thought they had discovered a new musical instrument.
lore.legendary: Floppimus carried the final save of a legendary adventure through forty years of forgotten drawers. When it was loaded again, the pixel hero asked why dinner was so late.

names.legendary: Fusarius, Keeper of the Final Spark

lore.common: Lives in a cupboard nobody remembers exists. The entire household visits it whenever the lights go out.
lore.uncommon: Trips whenever the kettle and toaster quarrel. They have never resolved their differences.
lore.rare: Can hear a faulty circuit through the walls and stops it before the first spark. Also refuses to power the karaoke machine.
lore.epic: Silenced an entire town's electrical grid during the grand fireworks countdown. The stars put on a better show instead.
lore.legendary: The oldest fuse box was built to guard a single spark stolen from lightning. Every storm it clicks three times, and the clouds answer.

names.legendary: Luminix, the Star in a Tube

lore.common: Cracks its little neck to start glowing and immediately demands the darkest corner at the party.
lore.uncommon: Glows fiercely for an hour, then fades exactly when somebody needs to find their shoes.
lore.rare: Leaves shimmering trails behind dancers until the party looks like a nest of friendly fireflies.
lore.epic: Lit up the swimming pool in a thousand colours and convinced the moon it had competition.
lore.legendary: Luminix was born when a falling star became trapped in a little plastic tube. Its light lasts only one night, but every dawn the star remembers how to shine again.

names.legendary: Luminax, the Third Eye of the Mountain

lore.common: Blinds everyone its wearer turns to speak to, including the wearer in a mirror.
lore.uncommon: Tightens its elastic strap just enough to leave a heroic stripe across the forehead.
lore.rare: Finds a hidden tunnel behind a cave wall while its wearer is busy eating a sandwich.
lore.epic: Lit a lost expedition's way through a crystal cavern, and every crystal sent its light across the valley. The village thought dawn had arrived.
lore.legendary: Luminax's light shines only on paths that lead safely home. A lost caver followed it for seven nights and emerged holding the mountain's oldest secret: a very sleepy bat.

names.legendary: Voxwell, Speaker of the Seven Doors

lore.common: Turns every visitor into a crackling robot, including Grandma carrying the cake.
lore.uncommon: Buzzes the door open one second after the delivery driver has walked away.
lore.rare: Imitates every resident's voice so convincingly that the postman gets invited to three dinners at once.
lore.epic: Connected an entire apartment block into one giant conversation. By midnight the neighbours had formed a choir and voted on the pizza toppings.
lore.legendary: Voxwell spoke through seven locked doors to warn a sleeping city of a rising flood. Every household heard a familiar voice calling them to higher ground.

names.legendary: The Wandering Wick of No Return

lore.common: Bounces its little pool of light across the path and makes every pebble look suspicious.
lore.uncommon: Walks ahead of its owner as if the lantern is taking itself for an evening stroll.
lore.rare: Leads anyone following its moving circle back to the same tree, no matter which path they choose.
lore.epic: Swung above the harvest procession and enchanted the entire village into following its golden circle into the duck pond. The ducks charged admission.
lore.legendary: The Wandering Wick travels the roads nobody remembers. It appears to those lost in the dark and lights their journey home, but never allows anyone to follow it back.

names.legendary: Orbulon, Dreamer in the Glass

lore.common: Needs an hour to wake up, then makes everyone else forget why they came into the room.
lore.uncommon: Floats its blobs up and down like little lava astronauts in a glass rocket.
lore.rare: Can hypnotise a cat with one slow bubble. The cat has been staring since Tuesday.
lore.epic: Sent enormous glowing wax shapes drifting through the nightclub, and the dancers moved in slow motion until dawn.
lore.legendary: Orbulon holds a pocket universe inside its coloured glass. Entire constellations drift between its rising globes, yet outside the lamp nobody can remember more than an afternoon passing.

names.legendary: Strobina, Herald of the Clear Road

lore.common: Turns every house blue for half a second as it passes on a vehicle's roof.
lore.uncommon: Blinks a mysterious rhythm that children try to copy from the pavement.
lore.rare: Flashes a warning so bright that even a distracted traffic cone stands to attention.
lore.epic: Lit the town's road-safety parade with a rhythm so irresistible that every crossing guard began directing traffic like a disco dancer.
lore.legendary: Strobina appeared on the first emergency wagon that dared drive through a burning city. Its blue beacon split the darkness into a safe passage, and the road still gleams faintly where it led.

names.legendary: Neonia, the Sign That Named the Stars

lore.common: Buzzes at the shopfront and makes the first letter blink like it is winking at customers.
lore.uncommon: Switches off one letter and turns a respectable diner into an accidental joke.
lore.rare: Paints the street pink, and every passer-by looks like they have a secret crush.
lore.epic: Rewrote all the city's rooftop signs in one brilliant night. Nobody could find the shops, but the skyline won an art prize.
lore.legendary: Neonia learned the secret language of lightning and trapped it in tubes of glowing glass. When the city goes dark, her letters still spell the names of those coming home.

names.legendary: Snugglebright, Warden of the Small Hours

lore.common: Glows in the corner but lets exactly one coat on a chair look like a ghost.
lore.uncommon: Dims itself whenever somebody tries to read under the blanket after bedtime.
lore.rare: Scares imaginary monsters away from beneath the bed, but invites the friendly ones to stay for stories.
lore.epic: Kept the nursery shining so warmly during a thunderstorm that the thunder stopped to listen to the bedtime story. The lightning waited outside.
lore.legendary: Snugglebright lit a path for every frightened child in the sleeping city on the longest night. In the morning its tiny glow faded, but no one remembered being afraid.

names.legendary: Aurawick, Keeper of the Last Harbour

lore.common: Coughs soot onto its own glass and then complains the world has gone dark.
lore.uncommon: Hums at passing moths until they form a disappointed queue beneath it.
lore.rare: Its flame points towards the safest path through a fog, even when the road signs disagree.
lore.epic: Marched through a ghost town lighting each abandoned window. The shadows fled into the well and argued over who had first seen a match.
lore.legendary: On the night every lighthouse failed, Aurawick burned aboard a little fishing boat. Its glow was seen across seven storms, leading an entire lost fleet home on one spoonful of oil.

names.legendary: Lumilla, Keeper of a Thousand Wishes

lore.common: Tears its delicate side on the first branch it passes and calls it ventilation.
lore.uncommon: Bobs over the picnic table like a tiny moon with a serious fear of raindrops.
lore.rare: Brightens whenever someone makes a promise they secretly intend to break.
lore.epic: Gathered a hundred garden lanterns into a glowing procession that drifted through the empty town. Even the streetlights turned to watch.
lore.legendary: Lumilla carried the wishes of a thousand children through the darkest night of the year. At dawn she returned with her paper unburnt and a firefly for every child.

names.legendary: Volta Pin, Guardian of the Last Spark

lore.common: Refuses to fit the socket until its owner kneels down and begs.
lore.uncommon: Lies pins-up on the carpet like a trap for unsuspecting toes.
lore.rare: Keeps power flowing through a storm that silences every other socket in the house.
lore.epic: Pulled itself out during the championship bake-off, stopping every oven mid-cake. The judges were forced to invent a new category: raw ambition.
lore.legendary: Volta Pin carried the last living spark through a powerless winter, passing it safely from house to house. The village still leaves one candle alight in its honour.

names.legendary: Ampereaux, the Last Sparkkeeper

lore.common: Has four glowing dots and only enough charge to tease a desperate phone.
lore.uncommon: Drinks the final battery bar from the owner's phone and calls it a loan.
lore.rare: Steals power from abandoned chargers and revives dead phones just before their alarms ring.
lore.epic: Devoured every charging cable at a music festival. The crowd made a human chain to power its glowing grin.
lore.legendary: Ampereaux guarded a single ember of electricity during the Great Blackout. One spark restarted the city, but it still charges people for borrowing a cable.

names.legendary: Multiplexa, Mother of a Million Plugs

lore.common: Already has six things plugged in, and none of them belong to you.
lore.uncommon: Turns its master switch off whenever someone says the document is almost saved.
lore.rare: Grows one new socket each night, but each socket wants its own expensive adapter.
lore.epic: Sprouted a hundred outlets beneath the office desks and tangled the entire staff into a cable-knit sweater.
lore.legendary: Multiplexa once connected every lighthouse on the coast through one impossibly long power strip. Sailors swear its red switch still glows beneath the sea.

names.legendary: Glintara, Star of the Midnight Road

lore.common: Blinks dramatically from the bicycle wheel whenever a car passes.
lore.uncommon: Collects every passing headlight and spends the whole ride showing off.
lore.rare: Sends a beam of light back through fog, showing lost cyclists the bend ahead.
lore.epic: Reflected a meteor shower so brightly that the entire night-time parade rode beneath a road of shooting stars.
lore.legendary: Glintara guided a caravan across a moonless desert by reflecting a single distant campfire. The travellers gave it a silver wheel that still shines after dark.

names.legendary: Halitella, Lantern of the Salt Caves

lore.common: Glows softly in the corner while everyone asks whether it is actually switched on.
lore.uncommon: Absorbs so much damp that it starts weeping pink tears onto the sideboard.
lore.rare: Calms an entire room with its amber glow, except for the cat, which insists the light is judging it.
lore.epic: Lit an office meeting with such deep tranquillity that everybody stopped arguing and adopted a pot plant as the new manager.
lore.legendary: Halitella was cut from a rose-coloured salt crystal beneath an ancient mountain. On dark nights she glows with the memory of the sea that once covered the stone.

names.legendary: Rewindra, Ghost of the Magnetic Choir

lore.common: Eats the tape precisely when somebody says this is their favourite song.
lore.uncommon: Needs a pencil to wind its tangled ribbons back into order and considers this collaboration.
lore.rare: Copies a song onto a blank cassette, but replaces one lyric with an embarrassing secret.
lore.epic: Played a forgotten concert through a hundred speakers at once, and the musicians stepped out of the magnetic tape to take an encore.
lore.legendary: Rewindra keeps the last recording of songs no living throat remembers. When her reels turn beneath a full moon, even broken instruments sing their missing notes.

names.legendary: Thermogard, Master of the Seventh Season

lore.common: Turns the heating up whenever someone opens a window, purely out of stubbornness.
lore.uncommon: Clicks at precisely the moment everybody starts to fall asleep.
lore.rare: Changes the living room to midsummer while the hallway stays in deep winter. The cat owns several coats now.
lore.epic: Overruled every other thermostat in the apartment tower, giving each floor a different season. The lift became a weather forecast.
lore.legendary: Thermogard guards the secret degree between winter and spring. Long ago he released it to save a frostbound orchard, and the trees have bloomed one day early ever since.

names.legendary: Luxara, the Torch That Found the Moon

lore.common: Goes dim precisely when you notice a suspicious noise behind the bins.
lore.uncommon: Eats fresh batteries and produces one feeble little circle of light.
lore.rare: Tracks hidden spiders across the garden like a detective chasing eight-legged criminals.
lore.epic: Sent a searchlight across the sleeping countryside and revealed an entire secret festival of nocturnal animals. The owls demanded privacy.
lore.legendary: Luxara guided the first explorer through a cavern that had never seen daylight. Her beam found the moon reflected in a black lake, and the cavern's blind fish learned the shape of stars.

names.legendary: Vinyluna, the Unending Chorus

lore.common: Skips exactly on the singer's favourite word.
lore.uncommon: Wobbles on the spindle until every ballad sounds mildly seasick.
lore.rare: Scratches an unheard harmony into the empty space between tracks.
lore.epic: Spun free of its turntable and carried an entire dance floor around the room like a glittering flying saucer.
lore.legendary: Holds the final song of a vanished orchestra within one endless groove. Play it at dusk and their music fills the hall, right down to the percussionist's sneeze.

names.legendary: Webcassandra, the Face of Tomorrow

lore.common: Finds the least flattering possible angle for every video call.
lore.uncommon: Freezes a smile halfway into a sneeze and refuses to apologise.
lore.rare: Shows the cat's true whereabouts whenever the meeting goes suspiciously quiet.
lore.epic: Turned an entire online school assembly into kittens wearing ties. The head teacher spent forty minutes trying to mute the purring.
lore.legendary: Captured a conversation that had not happened yet, warning a village of a coming flood. Everyone listened because the recording also correctly predicted the mayor's terrible haircut.

names.legendary: Voltara, the Invisible Conductor

lore.common: Refuses to charge a phone unless it lies at a peculiar angle of exactly smug.
lore.uncommon: Slides the phone two millimetres away from the sweet spot during the night.
lore.rare: Pulls stranded batteries toward its invisible coil like ducklings following their mother.
lore.epic: Archon Coilheart filled an entire concert hall with invisible charging rings. Every phone woke up at 100%, and every hairdo stood straight up.
lore.legendary: Voltara heard the first spark between two distant magnets and learned to carry power without wires. She once lit a lighthouse from across the bay, simply by asking the moon to move closer.
